question: is a fixed amount of extra memory worth more as a shared, salience-selected stage that any faculty can read (nothing copied), or spread as private slots?
grid: K {12,24,48} x slots {40,80} x cross {0.25,0.50} x noise {0.3,0.6,0.9}, 36 cells, seed 40000 + cell index, 100 histories

primary.measure: total, paired by history, bootstrap 95% CI (4000 resamples)
primary.rule: PAYS: mean >= +0.05 and CI lower > 0; COSTS: mean <= -0.05 and CI upper < 0; else NEUTRAL. per cell, per arm.

secondary: stage_random - stage_single on total (does selection matter)
prediction: stage_single PAYS where noise 0.3 and cross 0.50 (it solves addressing); local_plus wins (stage COSTS or NEUTRAL) at noise 0.9; temporal does not beat single on revision
seen_before: packet C's result (copying stage never pays) and grid-c2-check (seed 1, 3 histories) shaped this design, not these rules; seeds not reused
